mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Draft / Letter of Intent from the incorporating jurisdiction)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar) or Corporations Canada (if federal)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille – Canada is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; authentication by Global Affairs Canada or the Quebec competent authority applicable to the issuing registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Name Reservation / Name Search (Nuans or Quebec Name Declaration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (via the online registry) or Corporations Canada
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the country of origin, then Apostille by the competent authority (Global Affairs Canada or provincial designate), if the certificate is to be used outside Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Existence / Certificate of Status for Beneficial Owners (if a foreign company is the shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the beneficial owner's jurisdiction, or the Quebec Enterprise Registrar as agent upon request
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, if the counterparty is in a non-Hague country, consular legalization by the embassy/consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Identity and Address Proof of each Director and Shareholder (for FINTRAC and registry CDD purposes)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Government issuer (passport, national ID, driver's license) or regulated financial institution (reference letter)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy + Hague Apostille if the document is to be submitted to a Quebec notary for the declaration of immoveable or corporate attestation; otherwise internal verification by the registered agent is accepted

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) sanctions list, Global Affairs Canada sanctions regulations under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, United Nations Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN list (screening required by Canadian financial institution counterparties), and FINTRAC guidance on politically exposed persons (domestic, foreign, and international organization PEPs). Standard tiering: PEP triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds evidence, and senior management approval. Ongoing monitoring includes transaction pattern anomaly detection and registry cross-checks with the Quebec Enterprise Registrar and the federal Ultimate Beneficial Owner registry.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level_notes: The federal and Quebec registries maintain non-public government-access only beneficial ownership registers. Certain information may be disclosed with lawful authority to law enforcement, tax authorities, or financial intelligence units; public access to beneficial ownership in Quebec is limited to the name and address of the beneficial owner only upon ministerial authorization, and the register is not fully open to the public. Nominee shareholders are not categorically prohibited but nominee arrangements require full disclosure of underlying UBOs to the registry and financial institutions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online portal – https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca (Quebec Enterprise Registrar) and Corporations Canada's Nuans name search portal – https://www.ic.gc.ca/app/scr/cc/CorporationsCanada/nameSearch
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Quebec law requires a corporate name to be in French. A French-language name must include the legal element (e.g., 'inc.', 'ltée', 'corporation', or the French abbreviation). The name may include a French version and an English version; the French version must appear on all public documents. Transliteration doctrine: names in Latin script are accepted; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the roman alphabet. The following terms are reserved and cannot be used without ministerial authorization: 'bank', 'trust', 'insurance', 'university', 'college', 'association', 'commission', 'caisse', 'fédération', 'syndicat', 'corporation professionnelle', 'ordre professionnel', and any word suggesting governmental, quasi-governmental, or not-for-profit status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written request for review with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec within 30 days of the notice of rejection, stating the grounds for contesting the refusal and attaching a revised name proposal if applicable. An administrative review is conducted by a jurisdictional officer; if the review affirms the refusal, the applicant may either submit a corrected name or appeal to the Court of Quebec under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. For federal names, a similar reconsideration request may be filed with Corporations Canada within 30 days; an external appeal is available through the Federal Court. All filings must be submitted through the registry portal and must include the original name search report, the statutory declaration, and payment of the applicable fee. For Quebec incorporation, the name reservation is valid for 60 days; extensions may be requested for an additional 30 days upon payment of the extension fee before the expiration date.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the registered office of a Quebec business corporation, provided that the office is physically located in Quebec and is open to the public during normal business hours for service of process. A virtual office address (e.g., registered agent service) is acceptable if the agent maintains a physical Quebec street address and receives documents during business hours. However, for manufacturing activities (handmade resin dice casting), the Company must maintain a separate physical production location; the registered office need not be the production site. The Quebec Enterprise Registrar will accept a registered agent address as the registered office address. Commercial substance for tax and AML purposes requires the Company to demonstrate actual management, employees, and operational activities in Quebec; a mailbox-only arrangement without any physical or operational presence will likely be classified as a shell for Quebec tax purposes and may trigger enhanced scrutiny by Revenu Québec.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate (30-45%) – Revenu Québec and the Municipalité locale may conduct unannounced inspections to verify the enterprise's commercial presence, employee status, and compliance with municipal zoning and health-safety regulations. The likelihood increases if the registered office is a virtual office alone, if the company's declared revenue stream is high, or if the activity involves chemical handling (resin) without a dedicated production site. The probability of a desk-based document review is high (70-80%), while an actual physical site visit is more likely within 12 months post-incorporation if there are employee filings or GST/QST registrations.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; fixed CAD 32 for name search + CAD 32 for reservation; converted to USD at 1 CAD = 0.75 USD

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (CQLR c S-31.1), ss. 10-11 (articles), ss. 14-17 (certificate), ss. 19-22 (registered office), s. 30 (first directors), and s. 231 (written resolution).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (statuts constitutifs) filed under the Regulation respecting the Registraire des entreprises
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the QBCA; no escrow or capital deposit is required at incorporation. Authorized and issued capital may be denominated in any currency, and share consideration may include cash, future services, or property.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS

WHEREAS the Articles of Incorporation of the Corporation have been duly certified under the Quebec Business Corporations Act; and

WHEREAS the directors desire to implement the initial corporate governance measures;

BE IT RESOLVED:

1. The subscriptions, share allotments, and issuances of authorized shares to the initial shareholders listed in the subscription register are hereby ratified and confirmed.

2. The registered office is established at [ADDRESS], Province of Quebec, and the notice filed with the Registraire des entreprises is ratified.

3. The following directors are appointed as officers: [NAME] as President, [NAME] as Corporate Secretary, and [NAME] as Treasurer.

4. Management is authorized to open banking accounts, execute all required instruments, and incur expenditures incidental to this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - online name reservation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name search through the CID (Centre d'identification des entreprises) to verify legal availability. Submit to REQ a name reservation application containing a distinctive, descriptive, and legal corporate element. The reservation is valid for 90 days and must be used before filing the articles.
required_dossiers: List of proposed corporate names in order of priority
Power of attorney if a filing agent is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ refuses the name as confusing or not distinctive, file an amended name reservation with a different distinctive element, or request ministerial review through REQ's enforcement and examination service within 30 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and File Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Electronic Registration Centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in accordance with s. 10 of the QBCA, specifying share classes, limits on shares, maximum number of directors, and the initial registered office address. Submit the completed articles and the notice of registered office through REQ's electronic filing portal. Undertake publication as required by the Act by completing the statutory declaration.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate issued by REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues an 'avis d'irregularite' (notice of irregularity), cure the identified defects and resubmit within 15 days. If the articles are rejected after three attempts, prepare a corrected set and pay a new filing tariff.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Enterprise Register Attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, REQ issues a Certificate of Incorporation and enters the corporation in the Quebec enterprise register. Confirm that the legal name, jurisdiction, registered office, and director information are correctly reflected in the 'attestation' or extraction. Obtain an official extract for use in banking and enforcement matters.
required_dossiers: Official extract from the Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or extract contains clerical errors, file a rectification request with REQ within 30 days, attaching the relevant evidence and a written explanation of the error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Board Resolution and Minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors (internal act) under QBCA s. 231
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first board resolution either at a formal meeting or by unanimous written resolution. The board must pass the initial by-laws, confirm share subscriptions and allotments, fix the fiscal year end, ratify the registered office, elect officers, and authorize the opening of bank accounts.
required_dossiers: Share subscription forms and share register
Acceptance of office by directors and officers
By-laws adopted at the first meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director objecting to a resolution appears, the chair must record the dissent formally and, where legally available, obtain unanimous shareholder consent to ratify the action after due notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Account and Business Number Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with the CRA for a Business Number, GST/HST account, payroll source deductions, and corporate income tax account. Register separately with Revenu Quebec for QST and employer accounts. Use the CRA Business Registration Online portal and Revenu Quebec 'Mon dossier entreprise' portal.
required_dossiers: Directors' names, addresses, and social insurance numbers or business numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Quebec queries the registration, provide the supplemental authorization form and legal identification. Any duplicate or erroneous account may be consolidated by reporting the error to the assigned service officer.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for micro-scale manual dice casting; municipal building and fire authorities govern occupancy safety.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration tier (low-impact craft production). No full EIA is triggered for manual casting operations that emit fewer than 10 tonnes of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) per year and dispose of less than 50 kg of uncured epoxy waste per month.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No untreated process wastewater may be released to the aquatic environment. Air discharges must comply with the Clean Air Regulation (c. Q-2, r. 4.1). Municipal sewer discharges must meet the local by-law pH limits (6.0-9.5) and contaminant thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required from the local fire prevention department, addressing flammable resin storage, extinguishers, and exit signage. Structural load inspection must confirm casting tables and storage shelving can bear design loads. Workplace clearance under CNESST must verify adequate ventilation, hazardous substances identification, and ergonomic safety for casting operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada — federal GST/HST, customs-related excise, and federal corporate income tax; Revenu Québec — Quebec QST, Quebec corporate income tax, and employer/consumption taxes. Business registration portals: CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) via canada.ca/business-registration and Revenu Québec Business Registration (Cliquez d'affaires).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Business Corporation must first obtain a federal or Quebec certificate of incorporation, then procure a 9-digit Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account. Out-of-country persons register through CRA's Business Registration Online using form RC148 (Non-Resident Account Registration), or by mailing the completed GST/HST application form RC1 with a signed authorization and supporting corporate documents. Revenu Québec requires a separate QST registration (form VD or an integrated application via Cliquez d'affaires) and a Quebec enterprise number (NEQ). Mandatory documentary package for non-residents: certified certificate of incorporation, articles of continuance, director identification, and proof of a Canadian/foreign permanent establishment or agency relationship. If the non-resident corporation carries on business in Quebec without a permanent establishment, a registrant acting as fiscal representative or customs broker may be required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a `check-the-box` entity classification election for corporate law entities. The federal and Quebec Business Corporations are mandatorily taxed at the entity level. Available federal/Quebec elections relevant to a small gaming-manufacturing corporation include: (i) section 256(2) associated-corporation small business deduction election; (ii) section 85(1) rollover election on incorporation/asset transfers; (iii) section 89(11) capital dividend account election; (iv) section 104/105 trust-loss surrender elections if a beneficiary trust is used; (v) GST/HST quick method election (s. 170 and QST equivalent) for small suppliers; and (vi) hybrid-mismatch declarations under sections 18.4 and 18.5 of the Income Tax Act implementing BEPS Action 2, which disallow certain deductions where a foreign branch or hybrid instrument gives rise to a deduction/non-inclusion mismatch.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax — GST/HST (federal) and QST (Quebec Provincial Sales Tax / Taxe de vente du Québec), both VAT-type systems under the Excise Tax Act and An Act respecting the Quebec Sales Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies (net of capital property, goodwill and financial services) over any calendar quarter and the last four consecutive calendar quarters for GST/HST; a corresponding CAD 30,000 threshold applies for QST. A non-resident registered for GST/HST is automatically liable for QST if carrying on a commercial activity in Quebec and its taxable sales in Canada exceed the threshold. Separate mandatory-registration triggers apply to imports, digital-economy marketplace vendors (the substantial presence and excluded-supply rules) and any person who supplies taxable services in Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no national real-time fiscal-clearance or AES digital-stamping system; CRA requires electronic filing of GST/HST returns once registered, and prescribed invoice content under section 223 of the Excise Tax Act (e.g., supplier BN, date, consideration, total tax). Revenu Québec has introduced mandatory structured electronic invoicing (B2B) through the Quebec Business Integration and Revenu Québec Live (RL) platform under phased PEPPOL-based rollout from September 2025 for taxpayers with Quebec sales over CAD 50 million annually; small manufacturers of hand-crafted dice are not yet within the first mandatory phase and may transmit in PDF/A-3 with embedded XML voluntarily. All e-invoicing records must be retained for six years and made available for CRA/Revenu Québec audit on demand.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (a) a supply of tangible personal property (hand-crafted epoxy-resin RPG dice) made by the supplier that is exported 'as part of the supply' to a foreign destination, under section 6 of Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, and (b) a supply of a service made to a non-resident person where the service is not delivered or the supply does not arise in Canada, under section 7, provided the supplier keeps documentary evidence establishing the goods were exported within the required time. The QST rules mirror federal zero-rating under Divisions I and II of Schedule to the Quebec Sales Tax Act, requiring that the goods leave Quebec and the vendor be a QST registrant. Where dice are sold to foreign backers via Kickstarter or PayPal with overseas shipping addresses and foreign-sourced settlement funds, the supply may be zero-rated only if the supplier holds title, possession and risk until departure from Canada and records the shipment and payment in a per-backer order file.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form B13/G13 of the Canada Border Services Agency, transmitted through CARM — CBSA Assessment and Revenue Management — or courier CUSMA/automated manifest when export filing is required)
Bill of Lading or International Air Waybill issued by the carrier evidencing dispatch from Canada to the foreign consignee
Commercial Invoice with terms of sale (Incoterms), itemized product description, H.S. classification, quantity, final foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank/Payment-Service-Provider settlement record (Stripe, Kickstarter, PayPal payout reconciliation) evidencing foreign-sourced payment in original currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec impose strict substantiation audits for zero-rated exports; missing export documentation converts the supply to taxable at 14.975% combined, with net tax reassessed. Penalties include 10% of any unreported net tax for ordinary failure under section 285(1) of the Excise Tax Act, rising to 25% where a false statement was knowingly made, plus compound daily interest at the CRA prescribed rate. The normal four-year reassessment window is extended indefinitely where misrepresentation, neglect, wilful default or fraud is established, and both net-tax and income-tax reassessments can claw back tax credits and refunds for prior periods. Provincial QST infractions carry additional fines under the Quebec Tax Administration Act up to CAD 100,000 for deliberate falsification. Immigration, export-control, and money-laundering agencies may also refer fraudulent zero-rating schemes for criminal prosecution, involving seizure and restitution of the entire tax deferral.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), acting in coordination with the Department of Finance Canada for exchange-rate policy and monetary affairs; prudential supervision of Schedule I and Schedule II banks is vested in the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); anti-money-laundering and cross-border wire transaction supervision is administered by FINTRAC; non-bank payment service providers serving Canadian merchants are subject to registration with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full de jure and de facto convertibility on both current and capital account and accepts IMF Article VIII obligations. There is no exchange control, no central-bank approval requirement, no prior-approval licensing, and no restriction on importing equity capital, servicing trade payables, remitting dividends, or repatriating liquidation proceeds for a Quebec business corporation. Inbound and outbound payments settle freely through Canadian clearing systems in CAD or foreign currency. The only friction is tax compliance: Part XIII federal withholding tax at 25% applies to dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, commonly reduced to 5% or 15% under tax treaties such as the Canada-US convention; a parallel Quebec withholding regime under the Taxation Act (Quebec) may also apply to dividends paid by a Quebec-resident corporation to non-residents, with treaty coordination generally keeping the combined burden within treaty bounds. No currency-conversion timing constraint applies to profit remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory timeline: none. Canada imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion, repatriation, or retention ratio for export receipts. A Quebec exporter may maintain USD or EUR proceeds in domestic or foreign bank accounts, use them directly to settle import payables, or convert them to CAD at any time. The only reporting obligation is incidental and institution-side: FINTRAC requires every Canadian financial institution to report international electronic fund transfers equal to or greater than CAD 10,000; the corporate client must provide accurate purpose and beneficiary details but is not required to file any exchange-control declaration with the central bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating multi-currency account (CAD/USD) plus dedicated capital-escrow / crowdfunding-proceeds deposit account
Business Operating Account with Global Transaction Banking umbrella: USD concentration account, escrow deposit, and treasury-line eligibility
TD Business Deposit Account, USD business deposit account, and locked-in escrow deposit structure
Business operating account, USD clearing / FX package, and escrow account for reserved funds
Business operating and escrow deposit accounts
Corporate operating account and global transaction banking / FX treasury line

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Laurentian Bank of Canada (Banque Laurentienne du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Commercial operating account and escrow deposit product for Quebec SMEs

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Desjardins Group (Caisse Desjardins du Quebec, cooperative financial institution serving as the principal Quebec provincial treasury partner)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Business operating account and secured escrow / commitment account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High as a supplementary collection and disbursement rail, but Low as the sole or principal treasury bank for the Quebec corporation. Foreign electronic-money institutions such as Wise, Payoneer, or similar EMIs are not CDIC-insured deposit-takers and are not authorized to conduct banking transactions in Canada as chartered banks; they operate as money services businesses or as foreign payment service providers. Receiving Kickstarter/Stripe and PayPal payouts through a foreign EMI is legally workable for currency conversion and sub-account management, provided funds are swept daily to a Canadian Schedule I bank account and the EMI is registered with FINTRAC if Canadian-facing or is regulated in a FATF-equivalent jurisdiction. Under the current Retail Payment Activities Act transition, non-bank payment service providers serving Canadian merchants must register with the Bank of Canada; therefore, the blueprint should position the EMI as an overlay on the primary chartered-bank account rather than as the escrow or capital-account holder.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Quebec business corporation with foreign-resident directors, physical appearance at a Canadian branch is not a statutory requirement under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, but most Schedule I banks exercise discretion and may demand an in-branch interview for cross-border or crowdfunding-heavy profiles before activating international wire, FX, or treasury products. The customary mandate is a video-based identity interview for each signatory and beneficial owner combined with notarized or apostilled corporate documents; the Quebec Registraire des entreprises / Corporations Canada extract, articles, by-laws, banking resolution, register of directors and UBOs, FATCA/CRS self-certification, and government-issued photo identification are required. A Canadian resident authorized signatory can typically satisfy the in-person component in Montreal or Toronto, eliminating the need for all foreign directors to travel; however, if the sole director and UBO reside in a non-FATF or higher-risk jurisdiction, an in-branch meeting and an enhanced due diligence file will be imposed. Remote opening is feasible for a transparent Quebec-registered ISIC 3240 exporter with a clear UBO chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-resident ultimate beneficial owner with opaque accumulation of initial subscription funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated UBO register and organizational chart; shareholder subscription agreement and bank statements evidencing source of funds; salary and tax records or asset-disposal evidence; FATCA/CRS self-certification; criminal record check for each 25% or greater owner; written explanation of the commercial rationale for the foreign capital injection

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crowdfunding inflow classification (Kickstarter/Stripe) triggering high-risk e-commerce or crowd-funding underwriting flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kickstarter campaign terms and settlement reports; Stripe Payment Facilitation Agreement; board-approved disbursement plan; customer order, refund, and chargeback history; fulfillment and logistics contracts; certified financial projection linking inflows to work-in-progress inventory and production costs for sharp-edge epoxy-resin tabletop dice

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disbursements to Chinese resin, pigment, and mould suppliers creating perceived trade-based money-laundering exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed purchase orders and proforma invoices from suppliers; freight-forwarding and customs entry documents; translated supplier business licences; arm's-length pricing benchmark; proof of prior deliveries and inspection certificates; annual trade-flow reconciliation between purchase orders, invoices, and payments

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid inbound-offshore-outbound layering: equity or crowdfunding funds swept through Wise or Payoneer sub-accounts and paid to third-country beneficiaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-clearance treasury forecast and transaction-flow diagram; platform payout logs mapping each external wire to an underlying invoice or operating expense; bank-statement reconciliation; authorized-signatory and treasury-policy documentation setting maximum daily electronic-transfer values and beneficiary whitelists

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP ambiguity and misidentified controllers against OFAC or the Consolidated Canadian Sanctions list
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and PEP self-declarations for all directors and UBOs; automated and manual sanctions-screening results; passport copies; diplomatic or professional references where applicable; legal research memorandum on adverse media prepared by compliance counsel

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Kickstarter/Stripe and PayPal proceeds first settle with the US payment processor in USD; the compliant routing for a Quebec corporation is as follows: instruct Stripe or PayPal to remit by ACH or wire to the Canadian bank's US correspondent with the beneficiary identified as CA_CORP, the beneficiary bank as the Canadian Schedule I institution, and the purpose narrative set to CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / PRIVATE EXPORT REVENUE - ISIC 3240; use the bank's USD account or its SWIFT MT103 USD-clearing service through BMO, RBC, National Bank, or TD New York / Toronto trust branches; for equity injections by a non-resident shareholder, the wire credits the operating account and the covering board resolution constitutes the proof of equity contribution; no Bank of Canada or Canadian exchange-control approval is required; for amounts equal to or above CAD 10,000, the receiving institution generates a FINTRAC IETR report and the client must be ready to upload the platform settlement statement, commercial invoice, or share-subscription document; capital-escrow funds may be parked in the bank's deposit product until Kickstarter fulfilment milestones are achieved, with release executed by board resolution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For epoxy resin, pigments, and aluminium moulds sourced mainly from Chinese and Asian suppliers, the treasury blueprint prioritizes: SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for open-account trade settlements below the bank's large-credit threshold, each matched to a commercial invoice, packing list, and bill of lading; irrevocable at-sight or usance documentary letters of credit issued by the Canadian bank under ICC UCP 600 with MT700/MT710 messages for large first-time supplier orders, with the seller's bank as advising or confirming bank; CAD domestic disbursements for Quebec payroll and logistics through Payments Canada Lynx for large-value payments and ACSS for retail batch payments; USD disbursements through CHIPS or Fedwire correspondent clearing, or by converting an in-house USD balance to CAD at the Canadian bank's dealing desk; PayPal disbursements for direct-to-consumer digital-commerce refunds, with the PayPal balance reconciled daily to the operating account. No foreign-exchange-control approval is required for any outbound disbursement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward outrights in CAD/USD and CAD/EUR with tenors up to 24 months, transacted under an ISDA 2002 or bank-specific FX master agreement with credit support annex where the notional exceeds treasury limits.
FX swaps including overnight, tom-next, and spot-forward structures for short-term liquidity rebalancing between CAD and USD sub-accounts.
Cross-currency interest-rate and principal swaps (USD-CAD) for medium-term matched funding of production working capital, documented under IFRS 9 and supported by bank collateral arrangements.
Vanilla European-style FX options, both call and put, on USD/CAD for hedging uncommitted crowdfunding receivables, with premium paid in USD or CAD and mark-to-market reporting.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted-delivery currencies such as INR, BRL, and ARS booked offshore through a Canadian bank's foreign branch, used exclusively where no deliverable forward market operates for the underlying import currency.

Natural on-balance-sheet hedging through dedicated USD collection and disbursement accounts so that crowdfunding and US distributor cash inflows are directly offset against Chinese and USD supplier payables, minimizing outright derivative reliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) including director and shareholder information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation in each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties apply; persistent failure to file annual returns for two consecutive years may result in administrative dissolution by the Director, requiring court reinstatement with fees and possible tax consequences.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the corporation's fiscal year; if no fiscal year is set, the declaration is due by the registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing accrues monetary penalties under Quebec law; continued non-compliance may lead to administrative revocation of the enterprise registration and loss of legal capacity or corporate rights.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Maintenance and update of Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC Register) and accompanying disclosure if demanded under CBCA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (information retained in corporate records, not filed annually)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Update within 15 days after receipt of a notification of change; annual recall and compliance review recommended at fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain the ISC Register is an offence under CBCA; conviction may result in fines and disqualification; the register must be available for government inspection.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to distributing corporations, corporations whose articles or bylaws require an audit, or corporations where a shareholder or group of shareholders holding at least 5% of the voting shares demands a compliance audit. Non-distributing private corporations can dispense with the auditor by unanimous shareholder resolution under CBCA and Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Publicly accountable enterprises must apply IFRS; private corporations typically apply Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) under the CPA Canada Handbook; a Notice of Change in Accounting Framework is not required federally.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: CBCA requires every corporation to maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control, updated as changes occur; there is no separate annual online federal UBO filing. Any share transfer must be recorded immediately in the Register of Members, the board of directors must approve the share transfer by resolution, and stale share certificates must be cancelled. Quebec annual declaration must include accurate director, officer, and corporate information; share ownership percentages are not publicly filed with REQ for ordinary CBCA/Quebec corporations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control
Minute Book for shareholders and directors

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$150 – US$900 depending on registered agent, registered office, statutory mailing address, and virtual office provider in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$4,000 – US$15,000 for a small cast-resin RPG dice manufacturer; typical owner-managed private corporations waive the audit via unanimous shareholder resolution and replace with review engagement or compiled financial statements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general statutory rate (Federal 15% general corporate rate after 10% provincial abatement + Quebec 11.5% provincial general rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Small Business Deduction (SBD) reduces federal rate to 9% on the first C$500,000 of active business income of a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC); Quebec reduced SMB rate of 3.2% on the first C$500,000 of active business income, producing a 12.2% combined CCPC small business rate; additional federal Manufacturing and Processing (M&P) deduction further reduces qualifying manufacturing income to 8% federal, giving an approximate 11.2% combined rate for qualifying dice-production profits; Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) refundable credits may further reduce effective tax for qualifying casting-process experimentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; electronically filed through CRA-approved tax preparation software using GIFI financial data via the Canada Revenue Agency EFILE system (mandatory for corporate returns)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly corporate income tax instalments are due for CCPCs and other corporations when instalment base exceeds C$3,000
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return must be filed within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; balance of tax payable is due within 2 months after the fiscal year-end (3 months for a CCPC that was a CCPC throughout the prior taxation year and carried on business with taxable income; instalment payments due on monthly or quarterly basis under s. 157 Income Tax Act

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate name, legal address, 9-digit Business Number (BN), fiscal year start/end dates, registered province (Quebec), residency status, parent corporation identification, and industry classifier (NAICS 339930 - Doll, Toy, and Game Manufacturing for Tabletop Dice).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Check 'non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada'; enter Canadian PE locations and complete Schedule 91 to compute Canadian-source business income; a non-resident without a permanent establishment in Canada generally has no Part I T2 filing obligation unless disposing of taxable Canadian property.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income under GAAP (IFRS or ASPE) linked to GIFI schedules: sales from Kickstarter, Stripe, PayPal and wholesale channels; cost of goods sold including epoxy resin, sharp-edge moulds, polyhedral dice blanks, pigments, packaging; operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income reasonably attributable to the Canadian permanent establishment; transfer-pricing adjustments under s. 247 must be booked before Line 101; maintain branch accounts and functional currency elections.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after non-capital loss carry-forwards (Schedule 10), capital loss restrictions, and tax-basis adjustments; the CCPC SBD-active-business-income computation is made on Schedule 4.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim deductions only where the expense is incurred for the Canadian PE; treaty permanent-establishment attribution under Article 7 must be consistently applied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of Part I tax otherwise payable: 38% base rate minus 10% provincial abatement, minus 13% general rate reduction or 19% SBD (as applicable), leaving the 15% general rate or 9% SBD rate; foreign tax credits on Schedule 21.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation cannot claim the provincial abatement except for income taxable in a province; amounts taxable in Quebec trigger Quebec CO-17 reporting alongside the T2.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of non-resident status, ownership structure, 10%+ foreign shareholder disclosure, and Part XIII withholding balances for dividends and notional royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be attached to T2; failure to disclose substantial non-resident ownership attracts specified-shareholder anti-avoidance review and Part XIII assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; a repeat filer pays 10% plus 2% per month for up to 20 months; daily compound interest at CRA prescribed rate (base rate + 4 points) accrues on unpaid tax; failure to file can trigger arbitrary assessment under s. 152(7) and loss of loss-carry-forwards; repeated wilful non-filing is an indictable offence under s. 238 ITA.
